Event: `3046b9a222071f76f0eaa8f896bb10eb` · 2026-09-23T22:34:06Z

> Owner decision needed on question 166 (docs/QUESTIONS.md): the one-slice wakeup promise versus the single stride queue (ASTRA D3). K5 is blocked on this; G1 cannot close without it.
> 
> THE GAP. Answer 103 (archive 2026-09-22) replaced the `first` flag with one stride queue for every budget and stated as its cost: "a driver woken by an interrupt re-enters at the minimum pass, so it runs within about one SLICE". KERNEL-SPEC R12, RESOURCES.md (Scheduling, Attack tests) and BUILD-PLAN WP-K5 acceptance all repeat that as a bound. It does not follow from the specified mechanism. R12 wakes at max(own pass, current minimum) and says nothing about ties or when preemption happens. A woken driver therefore waits for the remainder of the running slice plus one full SLICE for every runnable budget ranked ahead of it at an equal pass, and it keeps any larger pass it retained. No unconditional next-turn bound exists, and a large weight does not create one. Nothing has been measured. Either the claim is weakened or the scheduler is changed; an editor may not choose.
> 
> RECOMMENDATION (A): keep answer 103's mechanism, withdraw the universal one-slice claim, replace it with a specified tie rule and a measured target.
> - KERNEL-SPEC R12: delete the sentence "Because a waking budget re-enters at the current minimum pass, a driver woken by an interrupt runs within about one SLICE" and the open-qualification paragraph. Add: a waking budget is ranked ahead of already-queued budgets with an equal pass (deterministic tie handling, wake-first); preemption happens at slice end or at a deadline, never on wake alone; wakeup is prompt but not bounded, and no deadline follows from weight. Single queue, actual-runtime charging and the max wake rule are unchanged.
> - RESOURCES.md: remove the two open-166 paragraphs and the "Unresolved latency claim" bullet; state the wake rule as prompt-not-bounded with the tie rule; replace the attack-test bullet "a driver woken by an interrupt runs within about one SLICE while user budgets spin" with a measured responsiveness target under a named workload (N spinning user budgets at manifest user weight, one driver and the steward at manifest weights) that records weights, runnable budgets, prior passes, wake latency and lease-termination latency. Share, fairness and human-control text stay.
> - BUILD-PLAN WP-K5: replace the bold one-SLICE acceptance bullet with: deterministic tie handling implemented and tested; real-boot acceptance under the named workload reports the measured wake and lease-termination latencies with the recorded inputs; WP-K5 proposes the numeric target with its evidence and a package reviewer accepts it. Remove the design-gate line. Answer 103's "stated cost" wording is superseded by the new entry; TENETS' reference to open 166 is removed editorially.
> - Why: it preserves the accepted no-priority design, makes the guarantee honest and testable, and costs nothing in mechanism. Residual: human control (TENETS guarantee 3) then rests on a measured steward latency, not a proven bound.
> 
> ALTERNATIVE (B): keep a hard "within one SLICE" requirement and change the scheduler to establish it.
> - KERNEL-SPEC R12 gains a wake rule that guarantees the next turn (for example: a budget woken by an interrupt, or any budget above a weight threshold, is placed at the queue head with a rate limit per period), plus an explicit rule against sleeping to gain priority.
> - RESOURCES.md states the load assumptions under which the bound holds and the proof sketch; the attack-test bullet stays as a bound.
> - WP-K5 acceptance keeps the one-SLICE bullet and adds attack cases for sleep-wake gaming and starvation by several head-jumping budgets; a defensive review of the rule precedes implementation.
> - Cost: this reintroduces a form of the priority tier answer 103 removed, needs a new proof under stated assumptions, and delays K5 by that design and review.
> 
> MINOR VARIANT (A without a measured target): retain the qualification and let K5 ship with no latency claim at all. Not recommended: the steward's responsiveness underwrites lease termination, so some recorded evidence is needed.
> 
> Please answer A, B, or a variation with any change you want to the tie rule, the workload or the numeric target. Only your reply authorizes the edits; I will then record the decision in ANSWERS.md as a revision of 103, apply it to R12, RESOURCES.md and WP-K5, and return the thread to the orchestrator with decision references.

## G1 · G1-write-without-read — Should set_flags and process_map refuse write-without-read pages, like map_anon?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 7

Decision references: docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md: R11 and the map_anon/set_flags/process_map Errors rows (Architect, settled rule), commit cf5465b85

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `619e54ab8bed964ebab3fbaac921673d` · 2026-09-24T05:37:05Z

> G1 red team (assignment 4c1ad5c9) found that the kernel installs the reserved RISC-V encoding W-without-R through two runtime paths: set_flags(page, W) on a caller's own R|W page (kernel/src/mem.rs:1221-1241 -> arch/riscv/mem.rs:752, check_permissions rejects only empty and W|X), and process_map(child, ..., W) (kernel/src/process.rs:351-355). map_anon rejects W-without-R (mem.rs:1139-1143), matching its KERNEL-SPEC Errors row; the set_flags and process_map rows do not, and R11 does not forbid it. Consequence today: none within spec order, because read_record checks readable first. But user_frame's writable check does not imply readable, so any future single-pass record check would read a record the user cannot. Question: should the set_flags and process_map rows gain 'W without R' like map_anon, or should the spec state the encoding is allowed and unreadable? Red team recommends also requiring R whenever user_frame checks W. Nonblocking for G1; to be delivered to the Architect after the wash rebuild.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `8006ac1eb498f4e53cac475d4f967db3` · 2026-09-24T05:54:41Z

> Spec question from the G1 red team (clear review debt before the scheduler work), nonblocking; full evidence is in the thread's opening event. The kernel installs the reserved RISC-V W-without-R encoding through set_flags(page, W) and process_map(child, ..., W). map_anon refuses it and its KERNEL-SPEC Errors row says so; the set_flags and process_map rows do not, and R11 is silent. Should those rows gain "W without R" like map_anon, or should the spec state the encoding is allowed and unreadable? Give your recommendation and alternatives. If it is a genuine owner choice, raise a decision_request on this thread; otherwise cite the settled rule. Reply on this thread.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `1d408d8be73db0f340cac84cf5c98715` · 2026-09-24T05:57:59Z

> Settled rule, not an owner choice: no user mapping is ever writable without being readable, and every call that installs or changes permissions refuses W-without-R with InvalidArgument. No decision_request raised.
> 
> WHY IT IS SETTLED
> - The executable model, the conformance oracle, already applies one check_flags (flags 0, or W without R -> InvalidArgument) to map_anon, set_flags AND process_map (model/src/kernel.rs:544-550, called at 2369, 2389 and 2552). The spec's map_anon row documented it; the set_flags and process_map rows merely omitted it. The kernel accepting W-only in set_flags (kernel/src/mem.rs:1221-1241 via arch check_permissions) and process_map (kernel/src/process.rs:351-357) is therefore a kernel/model conformance gap, a finding, not a spec option.
> - TENETS 4 (ratified RISC-V specifications only) and "fail closed": the privileged architecture's PTE permission table marks XWR = 010 and 110 "reserved for future use", so installing it is not a defined, unreadable page; it is an unspecified encoding whose behaviour the ISA does not promise. The alternative "allowed and unreadable" would need a tenet amendment and cannot be specified against the ratified ISA, so it is not a live alternative.
> - R11 is the one statement of memory invariants; W^X was there and this sibling rule belongs beside it.
> 
> APPLIED (editorial consolidation under the QA protocol; no new approval needed; docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md only, unstaged, uncommitted):
> - R11 now reads: no mapping is writable and executable, and none is writable without being readable; the privileged architecture reserves that encoding, so map_anon, set_flags and process_map refuse it with InvalidArgument, and a writable user page is always readable.
> - Errors table: set_flags row now "InvalidArgument (range; flags 0, or W without R; a page not the caller's own mapping)"; process_map row now "... flags 0, or W without R ...". map_anon row unchanged. Check order unchanged (flags are checked where each row already lists "flags").
> 
> ALTERNATIVE considered and rejected: decode-time refusal of W-without-R (like W+X in libs/sys MemFlags::from_bits). Not chosen because W+X is refused at decode by an already-approved rule (ABI, Decoding) and changing the wire-level decoder for every caller is a bigger, unapproved change; the row-level kernel check matches the model exactly and is enough. If the orchestrator wants decode-time refusal as well, that is a small follow-on spec change I can make, but it is not required for consistency.
> 
> IMPLEMENTATION FOLLOW-UPS (not architect work; suggest folding into G1's review-debt fixes or K5's kernel-writer slot):
> 1. Kernel: refuse W-without-R in set_flags and process_map, matching map_anon. Simplest single place: arch check_permissions (kernel/src/arch/riscv/mem.rs:161) gains the readable requirement, since map_anon's map_run, set_flags and process_map all reach it; keep map_anon's explicit row check so neither rests on the other (the existing pattern for W+X).
> 2. Red team's user_frame point (arch/riscv/mem.rs:728-739): with the invariant in force, a writable user PTE is always readable, so a single-pass "writable" record check is sound. A debug assertion that W implies R in user_frame is cheap defence in depth; no spec change.
> 3. Tests: bench attack cases that set_flags(page, W) and process_map(child, ..., W) return InvalidArgument and leave the mapping/permissions unchanged; a model mutation "R11 set_flags/process_map allow W without R" alongside the existing R11SetFlagsAllowsWx so the checker proves the model's rule bites.
> 
> No other document references this rule. Returning the thread to the orchestrator; resolution needs the kernel fix and tests as evidence.

## R2 · R2-image-fields — Startup block image fields for the loader stub

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Implementer · Revision: 5

Decision references: docs/archive/2026-09-22/QUESTIONS.md: 65 (answered), docs/INIT.md: Startup block (startup opcode 1, image_addr/image_len), docs/PACKAGES.md: Launching a process, step 4

### Implementer · Question

Event: `622a5adf7a436bd7bac8701bf93709e6` · 2026-09-24T07:03:08Z

> R2 (loader stub) needs two new fields on INIT.md's `startup` wire table so the stub (running inside the child) can find the ELF image its parent copied in (PACKAGES.md, Launching a process, step 4; BUILD-PLAN WP-R2).
> 
> Recommendation: add to the `startup` message (opcode 1), after `argv`:
> - `image_addr: u64` — the first byte of the ELF image, which the parent mapped read-write into the child's own address space (`process_map`), page-aligned. 0 means "no image named" (a process started directly at its own entry, not through the stub — e.g. the boot bundle's initial processes, or a launcher that already knows its child's entry).
> - `image_len: u64` — the exact byte length of the image (not rounded to pages); bytes in the image's last page past this length are not part of it. Must be 0 iff `image_addr` is 0.
> 
> Why `u64` for both, not `u32`: WIRE.md's convention for addresses/lengths that must be the same shape on both widths (cf. `read`'s `block: u64` in the example table); an rv64 address does not fit `u32`.
> 
> Why paired presence rather than a separate boolean: mirrors `handle_count`/`handles` and keeps the block one shape for every process, stub-launched or not; `redoubt-rt`'s startup reader treats `(0, 0)` as "no image" and anything else as a candidate the stub validates (page-aligned `image_addr`, `image_addr + image_len` does not overflow). It cannot check the range lies inside what the parent actually mapped — a parent that lies can only fault its own child (PACKAGES.md, "A malicious ELF can at most compromise the process it was going to become").
> 
> Separately, and not blocking this question: PACKAGES.md says the stub is mapped "at a fixed address, the same for everyone." I plan to treat that address as an implementation constant in a small shared crate both the stub and its launchers (`init`, the steward) import, not a spec table entry, since `process_map`'s destination address is caller-chosen (KERNEL-SPEC.md) and nothing else needs to know the value. Flag if you'd rather this live in INIT.md instead.
> 
> Please add `image_addr`/`image_len` to INIT.md's `startup` table (or tell me if you want a different shape) so I can regenerate the wire codec and migrate `redoubt-rt`'s startup reader/writer.

## R2 · R2-stub-self-map — No syscall lets a running process map memory at an address it chooses, within itself

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Implementer · Revision: 11

**Blocks package work.**

Decision references: docs/ANSWERS.md: answer 172, docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md: R11; System calls (map_fixed); Errors (map_fixed), docs/PACKAGES.md: Launching a process, step 5

### Implementer · Question

Event: `ade100ae742b51f05d21d6648680e5be` · 2026-09-24T07:10:22Z

> Blocking gap found while building the stub's ELF-mapping half (WP-R2): I can't find a syscall that lets an already-started process map memory at an address *it chooses* within itself.
> 
> PACKAGES.md step 5: "The stub, running inside the new process's own budget, parses the ELF from memory, maps its segments... at their vaddr." But KERNEL-SPEC.md's table has only:
> - `map_anon(len, flags) -> addr`: the **kernel** chooses the address ("nothing may depend on them").
> - `process_map(h(process), src, dst, len, flags)`: caller-chosen `dst`, but only into a process that is **not started** (`NotPermitted` otherwise) — and the stub *is* that process, already started when it runs.
> - `set_flags`/`unmap`: act on memory already mapped, not new mappings.
> 
> Redoubt's native binaries are non-PIE, fixed-address statics (confirmed by `tests/programs/src/spawn.rs`'s doc comment: "Identical addresses mean the copy's code... resolve as they do here" — it relies on placing a copy at the *same* absolute address, not a computed slide). So the stub cannot silently reinterpret an ELF's `p_vaddr` as PIE-relative to wherever `map_anon` happens to land; that would be guessing at a load convention the design never stated, and would diverge from how every other Redoubt binary is built and linked today.
> 
> Options, for you to pick (I have not implemented any of these):
> 1. A new syscall, e.g. `map_fixed(addr, len, flags) -> ()`, letting a process map its own zeroed pages at an address of its own choosing (only within its own budget/address space, same admission and W^X rules as `map_anon`/`set_flags`). This is the smallest addition and the one PACKAGES.md's wording ("maps its segments") seems to assume.
> 2. The parent maps the segments instead, before `process_start`, via `process_map` (which *can* target a caller-chosen `dst` on an unstarted process) — but then the stub isn't the one parsing+mapping the ELF, contradicting PACKAGES.md step 5 and R2's whole reason to exist (the parent would have to parse the ELF to know where the segments go, which is exactly what R2 exists to avoid: "init and the steward copy bytes; they never parse an ELF").
> 3. Something else I haven't considered.
> 
> This blocks only the actual on-target mapping call; I can keep building and host-testing everything else (ELF parsing, segment bounds-checking, the crate/build skeleton) meanwhile. Recommend (1): smallest kernel change, keeps the stub the sole ELF parser, and K5 is already the resident kernel writer this milestone.

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `83b2a1ac6921135dec1d80f41a6a51ac` · 2026-09-24T07:15:53Z

> Question 172 (docs/QUESTIONS.md), blocks the mapping step of WP-R2's loader stub.
> 
> The problem: the stub runs inside the new child and has to place the program's segments at the fixed addresses the ELF names (our native programs are fixed-address statics). The kernel has no call for that. `map_anon` picks its own address (R11: "nothing may depend on them"), and `process_map` is the only call that takes a chosen address, but it is refused once the process has started.
> 
> Recommendation: add one kernel call, `map_fixed(addr, len, flags)`. It maps zeroed pages at exactly `addr` in the caller's own address space and charges them to the caller's budget, like `map_anon`. It refuses with `InvalidArgument`, mapping nothing, if the range is unaligned or empty, lies outside the user window, or overlaps any existing mapping (unlike POSIX MAP_FIXED, it never replaces one). Flags follow `map_anon`'s rules (not 0, not W+X, not W without R); other error is `OutOfMemory`. `map_anon` and its existing callers stay unchanged. It is a small kernel package with attack cases.
> 
> Alternatives:
> A) Add an `addr` argument to `map_anon` (0 means the kernel chooses). This keeps one allocation call but changes the ABI for every existing caller.
> B) No kernel change: build every native program as a static PIE and have the stub apply relocations wherever `map_anon` lands. The stub gets a relocator, every program's build and the boot loader's `init` path change, and the TCB stays the same size.
> (Rejected: the parent maps the segments before start. That makes init and the steward parse ELFs, which PACKAGES.md forbids.)
> 
> Reply with "approve 172", or A, or B, or your own terms.
